name: Saab 340
summary: Swedish 30- to 37-seat regional turboprop with a low wing and a conventional low tail, flown by US regional carriers and now by cargo and charter operators.

wings: Low, straight wing with a slight taper
engines: Two General Electric CT7 turboprops in large nacelles slung from the low wing
Nacelles extend well aft of the wing's trailing edge
fuselage: Round, short regional fuselage with small oval windows
Rounded nose and a sloping windshield
Airstair door at the rear left; freighters have a large cargo door
tail: Swept fin with a dorsal fillet

tellTales: Regional turboprop with a low wing and a low horizontal tail
Two large nacelles reaching back behind the trailing edge
Short, round fuselage with a rounded nose and small oval windows

confusedWith.howToTell: The EMB-120 has a T-tail, a more slender fuselage and a longer pointed nose; the Saab 340 has a conventional low tail and a rounded nose.
The ATR has a high wing and a T-tail; the Saab 340 has a low wing and a low tail.
The 1900 is smaller with a T-tail and tail fins; the Saab 340 has a conventional low tail and a bigger, rounder fuselage.

usCount.source: FAA Releasable Aircraft Database — valid registrations
